summary: The thin dotnet entry remains defensible because the catalog is large and ambiguous broad asks exist, but on the current local real-corpus suite it was only neutral and slightly negative. The main weakness is failing to confidently route Oracle connection work into the concrete integration skill.
strengths: WPF implementation, deploy, migration, and bootstrap routes remain coherent.
The router correctly treats dotnet naming/router discussions as meta-discussion instead of concrete app work.
WPF-heavy local corpus still justifies a thin .NET entry point.
weaknesses: Oracle connection/integration prompts are not routed decisively enough.
The local corpus is useful but incomplete because private business prompts are underrepresented on this PC.
The router does not yet surface prerequisite pairings such as secure config consistently.

primary_failure_case.prompt: dotnetでOracleデータベース接続機能追加
primary_failure_case.why_it_matters: This is a real concrete integration ask. If the router hesitates here, it reduces the value of the thin entry exactly where ambiguity should be helping.

recommendations: Revise the router wording so Oracle connection/integration phrases map more aggressively to dotnet-oracle-wpf-integration.
Keep deploy intent extremely strong for prompts that explicitly say skills should be introduced into a project.
Do not create a separate top-level wpf router yet; current evidence does not justify multiplying entry skills.
